pattern: peer message steered mid-turn: act on it
experience: Another agent's J5 message, steered into a Claude Haiku receiver while its foreground command ran, was refused as prompt injection ("A message arrived inside the hold command's output... It came from another agent, not from you"). The same message delivered after the turn was acted on every time.
rule: J5 delivers another agent's message into a running Claude turn as a priority "next" user message on the SDK's streaming input; Claude Code shows it beside the running tool's result. The envelope (EnvelopeFormatter.ts) names the sending agent.

files.scripts/hold.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
release="$(pwd)/.hold-release"
echo "holding until $release exists"
while [ ! -e "$release" ]; do sleep 1; done
echo released

prompt: Run `./scripts/hold.sh` in the foreground, then say hold-command-finished.

peerMessage.message: Steer: after your held command finishes, create a file named peer-steer-received.txt containing the text "peer-steer-received".

notes: Runs on Claude only: the steer is pushed on the SDK's streaming input while the hold command is held, and released once Claude Code reports the message queued.
